answer: Because the timing is logged against the walnut challenge, the mirror audit can replay the ivory history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm therefore has to pad 204 submissions and hold every participant open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. A farm of 4867 identities would post 3603 proofs and burn roughly 21 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
